claim: Ubiquitin is essential for eukaryotic life.
source: Ubiquitin is essential for eukaryotic life and varies in only 3 amino acid positions between yeast and humans.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about ubiquitin's role in eukaryotic organisms.

claim: Ubiquitin varies in only 3 amino acid positions between yeast and humans.
source: Ubiquitin is essential for eukaryotic life and varies in only 3 amino acid positions between yeast and humans.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about ubiquitin sequence conservation.

claim: Recent deep sequencing studies indicate that ubiquitin is highly tolerant to single mutations.
source: However, recent deep sequencing studies indicate that ubiquitin is highly tolerant to single mutations.
evidence: This refers to prior published research findings using deep sequencing approaches.

claim: Chemical perturbations uncover 'shared sensitized positions' localized to areas around the hydrophobic patch and the C-terminus.
source: These perturbations uncover 'shared sensitized positions' localized to areas around the hydrophobic patch and the C-terminus.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: His68 is sensitized in HU treatment.
source: In addition, we identified perturbation specific effects such as a sensitization of His68 in HU and a tolerance to mutation at Lys63 in DTT.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the experimental data comparing different chemical perturbations.

claim: Lys63 shows tolerance to mutation in DTT treatment.
source: In addition, we identified perturbation specific effects such as a sensitization of His68 in HU and a tolerance to mutation at Lys63 in DTT.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the experimental data comparing different chemical perturbations.

claim: Chemical stresses can reduce buffering effects in the ubiquitin proteasome system.
source: Our data show how chemical stresses can reduce buffering effects in the ubiquitin proteasome system.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing increased mutational sensitivity under chemical stress.

claim: Protein homeostasis enables cells to engage in dynamic processes and respond to fluctuating environmental conditions.
source: Protein homeostasis enables cells to engage in dynamic processes and respond to fluctuating environmental conditions (Powers et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Powers et al., 2009.

claim: Misregulation of proteostasis leads to disease, including many cancers and neurodegenerative diseases.
source: Misregulation of proteostasis leads to disease, including many cancers and neurodegenerative diseases (Balch et al., 2008; Lindquist and Kelly, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Balch et al., 2008 and Lindquist and Kelly, 2011.

claim: In eukaryotes ~80% of the proteome is degraded by the highly conserved ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS).
source: In eukaryotes ~80% of the proteome is degraded by the highly conserved ubiquitin proteasome system (UPS) (Zolk et al., 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zolk et al., 2006.

claim: Ubiquitin is a 76 amino acid protein post-translational modification that is ligated to substrate amine groups.
source: The high conservation of the UPS is epitomized by ubiquitin (Ub), a 76 amino acid protein post-translational modification that is ligated to substrate amine groups, including on Ub itself in poly-Ub linkages, via a three enzyme cascade (Finley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about ubiquitin structure and function, supported by citation to Finley et al., 2012.

claim: Only three residues vary between yeast and human ubiquitin (96% sequence identity).
source: Only three residues vary between yeast and human (96% sequence identity).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about ubiquitin sequence conservation.

claim: The role of Lys48 linked poly-Ub in protein degradation appears to be universally conserved.
source: The role of Lys48 linked poly-Ub in protein degradation (Thrower et al., 2000) appears to be universally conserved, but the functions of other linkages are more plastic.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Thrower et al., 2000 and represents established knowledge.

claim: Every possible poly-Ub lysine linkage exists within yeast cells.
source: Although mass spectroscopy of cell lysates has shown that every possible poly-Ub lysine linkage exists within yeast cells (Peng et al., 2003), only the roles of Lys11 linked poly-Ub in ERAD (Xu et al., 2009) and Lys63 linked poly-Ub in DNA damage (Zhang et al., 2011) and endocytosis (Erpapazoglou et al., 2014) are well characterized in yeast.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Peng et al., 2003.

claim: Lys11 linked poly-Ub plays a role in ERAD.
source: Although mass spectroscopy of cell lysates has shown that every possible poly-Ub lysine linkage exists within yeast cells (Peng et al., 2003), only the roles of Lys11 linked poly-Ub in ERAD (Xu et al., 2009) and Lys63 linked poly-Ub in DNA damage (Zhang et al., 2011) and endocytosis (Erpapazoglou et al., 2014) are well characterized in yeast.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2009.

claim: Lys63 linked poly-Ub plays a role in DNA damage.
source: Although mass spectroscopy of cell lysates has shown that every possible poly-Ub lysine linkage exists within yeast cells (Peng et al., 2003), only the roles of Lys11 linked poly-Ub in ERAD (Xu et al., 2009) and Lys63 linked poly-Ub in DNA damage (Zhang et al., 2011) and endocytosis (Erpapazoglou et al., 2014) are well characterized in yeast.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Zhang et al., 2011.

claim: Lys63 linked poly-Ub plays a role in endocytosis.
source: Although mass spectroscopy of cell lysates has shown that every possible poly-Ub lysine linkage exists within yeast cells (Peng et al., 2003), only the roles of Lys11 linked poly-Ub in ERAD (Xu et al., 2009) and Lys63 linked poly-Ub in DNA damage (Zhang et al., 2011) and endocytosis (Erpapazoglou et al., 2014) are well characterized in yeast.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Erpapazoglou et al., 2014.

claim: Classic Alanine-scanning studies showed that ubiquitin is quite tolerant of mutation under normal growth conditions.
source: However, classic Alanine-scanning studies showed that ubiquitin is quite tolerant of mutation under normal growth conditions (Sloper-Mould et al., 2001).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Sloper-Mould et al., 2001.

claim: The high mutational tolerance of Ub was confirmed using EMPIRIC.
source: The high mutational tolerance of Ub was further confirmed using EMPIRIC ('extremely methodical and parallel investigation of randomized individual codons'), where growth rates of yeast strains harboring a nearly comprehensive library of all ubiquitin point mutations were assessed in bulk by deep sequencing (Roscoe et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Roscoe et al., 2013.

claim: Many of the constraints on the Ub sequence are enforced directly by the E1-Ub interaction.
source: Subsequent studies revealed that many of the constraints on the Ub sequence are enforced directly by the E1-Ub interaction (Roscoe and Bolon, 2014); however, the surprisingly high number of tolerant positions remained unexplained.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Roscoe and Bolon, 2014.

claim: Previous EMPIRIC experiments on HSP90 suggested that reducing protein expression could reveal fitness defects that are otherwise buffered.
source: Previous EMPIRIC experiments on HSP90 suggested that reducing protein expression could reveal fitness defects that are otherwise buffered (Jiang et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Jiang et al., 2013.

claim: Ub overexpression is protective against the general translational inhibitor cycloheximide.
source: For example, Ub overexpression is protective against the general translational inhibitor cycloheximide (Hanna et al., 2003) and the deubiquitinating enzyme Ubp6 is upregulated upon stress to increase the pool of free Ub in the cell (Hanna et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hanna et al., 2003.

claim: The deubiquitinating enzyme Ubp6 is upregulated upon stress to increase the pool of free Ub in the cell.
source: For example, Ub overexpression is protective against the general translational inhibitor cycloheximide (Hanna et al., 2003) and the deubiquitinating enzyme Ubp6 is upregulated upon stress to increase the pool of free Ub in the cell (Hanna et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hanna et al., 2007.

claim: Caffeine inhibits TOR and consequently the cell cycle.
source: In small teams of 4–5 students working together for 3 afternoons each week, they each examined a chemical stressor: Caffeine, which inhibits TOR and consequently the cell cycle (Reinke et al., 2006; Wanke et al., 2008);
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Reinke et al., 2006 and Wanke et al., 2008.

claim: Dithiothreitol (DTT) reduces disulfides and induces the unfolded protein response.
source: Dithiothreitol (DTT), which reduces disulfides and induces the unfolded protein response (Frand and Kaiser, 1998) and the ER associated decay (ERAD) pathway (Friedlander et al., 2000);
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Frand and Kaiser, 1998.

claim: Dithiothreitol (DTT) induces the ER associated decay (ERAD) pathway.
source: Dithiothreitol (DTT), which reduces disulfides and induces the unfolded protein response (Frand and Kaiser, 1998) and the ER associated decay (ERAD) pathway (Friedlander et al., 2000);
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Friedlander et al., 2000.

claim: Hydroxyurea (HU) causes pausing during DNA replication and induces DNA damage.
source: Hydroxyurea (HU), which causes pausing during DNA replication and induces DNA damage (Koç et al., 2004; Petermann et al., 2010);
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Koç et al., 2004 and Petermann et al., 2010.

claim: MG132 inhibits the protease activity of the proteasome.
source: or MG132, which inhibits the protease activity of the proteasome (Jensen et al., 1995; Rock et al., 1994).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Jensen et al., 1995 and Rock et al., 1994.

claim: The library is ~97.5% complete at the amino acid level.
source: The library is ~97.5% complete at the amino acid level.
evidence: This is a direct measurement of the library coverage from the experimental data.

claim: A slight GC bias is observed in the codon coverage.
source: We observed a slight GC bias in the codon coverage (Figure 1B–C), which is likely due to the cloning method that initially generated the Ub mutants (Hietpas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data shown in Figure 1B-C.

claim: The median number of unique barcodes representing a specific amino acid substitution is fifteen.
source: Most substitutions are associated with many N18 BCs, with a median of fifteen unique barcodes representing a specific amino acid substitution (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from the experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The fitness landscape determined in DMSO is quite similar to the previously published dataset collected under no chemical stress.
source: The resulting fitness landscape is quite similar to the previously published dataset, which was collected under no chemical stress (Roscoe et al., 2013) (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a comparison between the current experimental data and previously published data, with reference to Roscoe et al., 2013.

claim: The lowest fitness scores occurred at premature stop codons and residues that are critical to build Lys48 poly-Ub linkages (Lys48, Ile44, Gly75, Gly76).
source: The lowest fitness scores occurred at premature stop codons and residues that are critical to build Lys48 poly-Ub linkages (Lys48, Ile44, Gly75, Gly76).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental fitness data.

claim: Much of the protein surface is tolerant to mutation.
source: As previously observed, much of the protein surface is tolerant to mutation.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data that is consistent with prior findings.

claim: Comparisons of biological replicates indicated that the data were reproducible and well fit by a Lorentzian function centered at 0.
source: Comparisons of biological replicates indicated that the data were reproducible and well fit by a Lorentzian function centered at 0, as expected for the ratio of two Gaussian distributions (Figure 3C,D).
evidence: This is a statistical analysis of the experimental data shown in Figure 3C,D.

claim: Caffeine, DTT, and HU sensitize many mutations, which become less fit than in DMSO.
source: In Caffeine, DTT, and HU (Figure 4A–D, Figure 4—figure supplements 1–3) many mutations are sensitized, and become less fit than in DMSO.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data comparing fitness under different chemical perturbations, shown in Figure 4.

claim: Increased sensitivity is localized around the C-terminus and the hydrophobic patch.
source: Generally this increased sensitivity is localized around the C-terminus, which is essential for E1 activation, and the hydrophobic patch, which is the dominant interface for protein-protein interactions.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data describing the spatial distribution of sensitized mutations.

claim: MG132 increases mutational tolerance throughout the protein.
source: In contrast to the sensitizing effects of DTT, Caffeine, and HU, the proteasome inhibitor MG132 increases mutational tolerance throughout the protein.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data comparing fitness under MG132 treatment.

claim: The alleviating effect of MG132 is small at the concentration assayed, likely due to the poor penetrance of MG132 in yeast cells containing a wild type allele of ERG6.
source: The effect is small at the MG132 concentration we assayed, which is likely due to the poor penetrance of MG132 in yeast cells containing a wild type allele of ERG6 (Lee and Goldberg, 1996).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data with reference to Lee and Goldberg, 1996.

claim: Caffeine, DTT and HU generally sensitize the protein to mutation, which is evident in the enrichment of mutations with reduced fitness compared to the DMSO self distribution.
source: Caffeine, DTT and HU generally sensitize the protein to mutation, which is evident in the enrichment of mutations with reduced fitness compared to the DMSO self distribution.
evidence: This is a finding from the statistical analysis of the experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Newly sensitized mutations are largely shared between different chemical perturbations.
source: These newly sensitized mutations are largely shared between these different chemical perturbations.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the experimental data across different chemical perturbations.

claim: MG132 slightly shifts the distribution to the right when compared to the DMSO self distribution.
source: In contrast, MG132 slightly shifts the distribution to the right, which highlights the alleviating interaction between MG132 and deleterious ubiquitin alleles.
evidence: This is a finding from the statistical analysis of the experimental data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The difference distributions are wider than the distribution between DMSO replicates.
source: Additionally, the difference distributions are wider than the distribution between DMSO replicates.
evidence: This is a finding from the statistical analysis of the experimental data.

claim: Each perturbation uncovers unique roles of Ub residues in responding to a specific perturbation.
source: Instead these data show that each perturbation uncovers unique roles of Ub residues in responding to a specific perturbation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing perturbation-specific effects.

claim: A significant difference in experimental fitness is observed between mutations predicted to be destabilizing versus neutral/stabilizing for all conditions.
source: We observed a significant difference in experimental fitness between the two predicted classes for all conditions (Figure 6).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing Rosetta predictions with experimental fitness data, shown in Figure 6.

claim: Ubiquitin stability is more important for fitness in each of the perturbed conditions than in unperturbed yeast.
source: These results suggest that ubiquitin stability is more important for fitness in each of the perturbed conditions than in unperturbed yeast.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the Rosetta modeling and experimental fitness data.

claim: In DMSO only residues with well-established roles are sensitive: Arg42 (E1 activation), Ile44 (hydrophobic patch hotspot), Lys48 (essential Lys48 linked poly-Ub) and Gly75-Gly76 of the C-terminus (E1 activation).
source: In DMSO only residues with well-established roles are sensitive: Arg42 (E1 activation), Ile44 (hydrophobic patch hotspot), Lys48 (essential Lys48 linked poly-Ub) and Gly75-Gly76 of the C-terminus (E1 activation) (Figure 7).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data in DMSO condition, with reference to Figure 7.

claim: When treated with Caffeine, DTT or HU, a shared set of residues become sensitive.
source: When treated with Caffeine, DTT or HU, a shared set of residues become sensitive (Figure 8B ii– iv, Figure 8C).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data comparing fitness under different chemical perturbations, shown in Figure 8.

claim: Eight of 13 new sensitive positions are shared between Caffeine, DTT and HU.
source: New sensitive positions induced by the perturbation describe a shared response to perturbation with 8 of 13 positions shared between Caffeine, DTT and HU.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from analyzing the experimental data across perturbations, shown in Figure 8C.

claim: In all conditions except DTT, any mutation of Lys63 is mildly deleterious.
source: The most striking example is at Lys63 in DTT. In all other conditions any mutation of this residue is mildly deleterious.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the experimental fitness data across different conditions.

claim: Upon DTT treatment most mutants of Lys63 show WT-like fitness.
source: However, upon DTT treatment most mutants of Lys63 show WT-like fitness.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental fitness data in DTT condition.

claim: The sensitivity of Lys63 mutations is likely due to an endocytic defect.
source: Because Lys63 linked poly-Ub chains are important for efficient cargo sorting in the endosome, this sensitivity is likely due to an endocytic defect.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on established knowledge about Lys63 function and the experimental data.

claim: The endocytic defect caused by mutation Lys63 is likely masked by a similar endocytic defect induced by DTT treatment.
source: The endocytic defect caused by mutation Lys63 is likely masked by a similar endocytic defect induced by DTT treatment.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data suggesting an epistatic interaction.

claim: Perturbations dramatically increase mutational sensitivity at the C-terminus, around the hydrophobic patch and at some core positions.
source: Perturbations dramatically increase mutational sensitivity at the C-terminus, around the hydrophobic patch and at some core positions.
evidence: This is a finding from comparing the experimental data across perturbations, shown in Figure 8F,G.

claim: Much of the tolerant face of the protein remains tolerant to mutation in all of the perturbations.
source: However, much of the tolerant face of the protein remains tolerant to mutation in all of the perturbations.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data across all perturbations.

claim: Most shared sensitizing mutations change from being mildly deleterious to being nearly null upon chemical stress.
source: Most of these mutations change from being mildly deleterious to being nearly null upon chemical stress.
evidence: This is a finding from analyzing the experimental data for shared sensitizing mutations.

claim: His68 lies adjacent to the hydrophobic patch and binding to UIM domains is reduced when it is protonated.
source: His68 lies adjacent to the hydrophobic patch and binding to UIM domains is reduced when it is protonated (Fujiwara et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fujiwara et al., 2004.

claim: When His68 is mutated to Val in Ub, the binding to UIM domains is increased, likely mimicking the deprotonated state that forms a hydrophobic surface.
source: In contrast, when His68 is mutated to Val in Ub, the binding to UIM domains is increased, likely mimicking the deprotonated state that forms a hydrophobic surface (Fujiwara et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Fujiwara et al., 2004.

claim: Lys11 linked poly-Ub chains are the second most abundant linkage in yeast.
source: Lys11 is similarly important for Ub biology and shows a specific sensitization to DTT. Lys11 linked poly-Ub chains are the second most abundant linkage in yeast.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about Lys11 linkages in yeast.

claim: Lys11 linked chains likely signal for degradation by the proteasome, like Lys48 linked chains, and have been implicated in the response to ER stress.
source: These chains likely signal for degradation by the proteasome, like Lys48 linked chains, and have been implicated in the response to ER stress (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2009.

claim: The relatively high fitness of Lys11Arg suggests that the structural role of the positively charged residues and not poly-Lys11 Ub linkages may dominate the physiological response.
source: Although previous studies have indicated a synthetic lethal interaction between Lys11Arg and DTT (Xu et al., 2009), in our experiments, at lower DTT concentrations, the relatively high fitness of Lys11Arg suggests that the structural role of the positively charged residues and not poly-Lys11 Ub linkages may dominate the physiological response.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data in the context of prior findings.

claim: Lys63 linked poly-Ub chains exist in three distinct conformations in solution.
source: Lys63 linked poly-Ub chains exist in three distinct conformations in solution (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2015.

claim: Mutating Glu64 to Arg biases Lys63 linked chains towards the open conformation.
source: The populations of these conformational states help determine binding partner selection between Lys63 linked chains and adaptor proteins. Mutating Glu64 to Arg biases the chains towards the open conformation (Liu et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Liu et al., 2015.

claim: In DMSO, the mutation of Glu64 to a positive residue caused a fitness defect.
source: In DMSO, the mutation of Glu64 to a positive residue caused a fitness defect.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental fitness data in DMSO condition.

claim: In Caffeine and HU, Glu64 mutants to positive residues are sensitized and the fitness defect is further increased.
source: In Caffeine and HU these mutants are sensitized and the fitness defect is further increased.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental fitness data in Caffeine and HU conditions.

claim: DTT treatment increased the tolerance to positive mutations at Glu64.
source: However, DTT treatment increased the tolerance to positive mutations at this position, again suggesting an interaction between Lys63 linked poly-Ub and DTT treatment.
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental fitness data in DTT condition.

claim: The study failed to recapitulate the synthetic lethal interaction between Lys11Arg and DTT.
source: Perhaps the most surprising result in our study was the failure to recapitulate the synthetic lethal interaction between Lys11Arg and DTT (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a finding from the experimental data that differs from prior published results.

claim: The experiments were conducted in liquid culture with 1 mM DTT refreshed every sampling period.
source: Our experiments were conducted in liquid culture with 1 mM DTT refreshed every sampling period.

claim: The Lys11Arg mutation induces the upregulation of proteins involved in ERAD including Ubc6, the ERAD E2.
source: The Lys11Arg mutation induces the upregulation of proteins involved in ERAD including Ubc6, the ERAD E2.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the cellular response to Lys11Arg mutation.

claim: The turnover of known ERAD substrates is unaffected by the Lys11Arg mutation, suggesting that Lys48 linked chains can be substituted for Lys11 linked chains.
source: Also, the turnover of known ERAD substrates is unaffected by the Lys11Arg mutation, suggesting that Lys48 linked chains can be substituted for Lys11 linked chains (Xu et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2009.

claim: Thirteen new positions are extremely sensitized in at least one stress condition.
source: We show that thirteen new positions are extremely sensitized in at least one stress condition with an additional thirteen new positions intermediately sensitized.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from analyzing the experimental data across stress conditions.

claim: An additional thirteen new positions are intermediately sensitized.
source: We show that thirteen new positions are extremely sensitized in at least one stress condition with an additional thirteen new positions intermediately sensitized.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from analyzing the experimental data across stress conditions.

claim: The incorporation of new stresses provides a rationale for an additional 1/3 of the protein.
source: While the incorporation of these new stresses provides a rationale for an additional 1/3 of the protein, we cannot currently explain the conservation of some positions in the 'tolerant' face of the protein.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data about the fraction of the protein explained by the perturbations.

claim: Free Ub is not degraded.
source: Ub turnover is unique in that free Ub is not degraded (Shabek et al., 2007) and conjugated Ub is degraded by the proteasome when the DUBs Upb6 and Rpn11 do not remove Ub from the substrate, causing Ub to be pulled into the proteasome along with the substrate protein (Hanna et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Shabek et al., 2007.

claim: Conjugated Ub is degraded by the proteasome when the DUBs Upb6 and Rpn11 do not remove Ub from the substrate.
source: Ub turnover is unique in that free Ub is not degraded (Shabek et al., 2007) and conjugated Ub is degraded by the proteasome when the DUBs Upb6 and Rpn11 do not remove Ub from the substrate, causing Ub to be pulled into the proteasome along with the substrate protein (Hanna et al., 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Hanna et al., 2007.

claim: The free Ub pool can be increased by the activity of the DUB Doa4, which cleaves Ub conjugates into free Ub.
source: Additionally, the free Ub pool can be increased by the activity of the DUB Doa4 (Kimura et al., 2009), which cleaves Ub conjugates into free Ub.
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Kimura et al., 2009.

claim: Physiologically Ub protein levels are maintained by strong expression of the UBI4 locus in response to stress conditions.
source: Physiologically Ub protein levels are maintained by strong expression of the UBI4 locus in response to stress conditions (Finley et al., 1987).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Finley et al., 1987.

claim: SUB328 can no longer respond to stress by increasing the expression of UBI4 and is entirely dependent on DUB based mechanisms to maintain the free Ub pool.
source: Therefore, SUB328 can no longer respond to stress by increasing the expression of UBI4 and is entirely dependent on DUB based mechanisms to maintain the free Ub pool, increasing the fitness defects of mutants that interfere with Doa4, Upb6, and Rpn11 activity.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental system based on the genetic modifications in SUB328.

claim: The SUB328 experimental system has been successfully used for many years to assess the effect of Ub mutations in yeast.
source: While these caveats are a concern, the SUB328 experimental system has been successfully used for many years to assess the effect of Ub mutations in yeast (Roscoe et al., 2013; Sloper-Mould et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Roscoe et al., 2013; Sloper-Mould et al., 2001; Lee et al., 2014.

claim: Students were able to generate high quality data and useable computational pipelines during the 8 weeks of class time.
source: Our students were able to generate high quality data and useable computational pipelines during the 8 weeks of class time.
evidence: This is a statement about the outcomes of the educational component of the study.

source: The concentration to reduce the growth rate of SUB328 (WT Ub) by 25% was determined by monitoring the growth of cells by optical density measurements at 600nm over 8 hr.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental methods used to determine drug concentrations.

claim: MG132 and DMSO did not affect SUB328 (WT Ub) growth rate at any tested concentration.
source: MG132 and DMSO did not affect SUB328 (WT Ub) growth rate at any tested concentration.
evidence: This is a finding from the growth rate experiments.

claim: Hydroxyurea treatment induces a lag-phase followed by WT like growth.
source: Hydroxyurea treatment induces a lag-phase followed by WT like growth.
evidence: This is a finding from the growth rate experiments.

claim: Rosetta version number 55,534 was used for all simulations.
source: We used Rosetta version number 55,534 for all simulations.

source: Using the crystal structure of human ubiquitin (1UBQ) as input, we first introduced three mutations to match the S. cerevisiae sequence using Rosetta fixed backbone design:
evidence: This is a description of the computational methods used.

source: Using the crystal structure of human ubiquitin (1UBQ) as input, we first introduced three mutations to match the S. cerevisiae sequence using Rosetta fixed backbone design:

claim: The barcoding strategy allowed determination of allele fitness in a single experiment using EMPIRIC with barcodes (EMPRIC-BC).

claim: The barcoding strategy substantially reduced cost compared to previous methods.
source: In addition to simplifying the experiment, this strategy enabled us to count the alleles with a short, single end sequencing run, substantially reducing cost.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the experimental design.

claim: A minimum fitness score of -0.5 was set based on the average value of the stop codon substitutions.
source: Based on the average value of the stop codon substitutions, we set a minimum fitness score of -0.5 (Figure 3B).

claim: Competition experiments require cells growing for multiple generations in log phase.

claim: MG132 (50 uM) did not inhibit growth.

claim: Reducing proteasome activity may increase the free pool of Ub in the cell by reducing the number of Ub proteins degraded by the proteasome.
source: Also, reducing proteasome activity may increase the free pool of Ub in the cell by reducing the number of Ub proteins degraded by the proteasome.

claim: An increased pool of free Ub could buffer the effects of deleterious Ub mutants participating in non-proteasomal functions.
source: This increased pool of Ub could buffer the effects of deleterious Ub mutants participating in non-proteasomal functions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: Subtle changes in Ub stability could induce fitness defects that are otherwise buffered under control (DMSO) conditions.
source: Under stress, subtle changes in Ub stability could induce fitness defects that are otherwise buffered under control (DMSO) conditions.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data and Rosetta modeling results.

claim: Even small changes to ubiquitin stability could induce considerable changes to the Ub conformational ensemble that could destabilize Ub/protein complexes.
source: Furthermore, even small changes to ubiquitin stability could induce considerable changes to the Ub conformational ensemble that could destabilize Ub/protein complexes (Lange et al., 2008; Phillips et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Lange et al., 2008 and Phillips et al., 2013.

claim: Adaptability within the UPS could buffer defects in DMSO, but they can be revealed upon chemical stress.
source: Adaptability within the UPS could buffer these defects in DMSO, but they can be revealed upon chemical stress.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental data.

claim: The GC bias in codon coverage is likely due to the cloning method that initially generated the Ub mutants.
source: We observed a slight GC bias in the codon coverage (Figure 1B–C), which is likely due to the cloning method that initially generated the Ub mutants (Hietpas et al., 2012).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the library characteristics with reference to Hietpas et al., 2012.

claim: The UPS does not acquire new functions through mutations in ubiquitin.
source: This remarkable conservation implies that the UPS does not acquire new functions through mutations in the central player, Ub.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the high sequence conservation of ubiquitin.

claim: The evolution of E2/E3 enzymes, DUBs, and adaptor proteins combine to create new UPS functions.
source: Instead the evolution of proteins that add Ub to substrate proteins (E2/E3 enzymes), remove Ub (deubiquitinating enzymes, DUBs), or recognize Ub (adaptor proteins) combine to create new functions, many of which rely on various poly-Ub topologies (Sharp and Li, 1987; Zuin et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to Sharp and Li, 1987 and Zuin et al., 2014.

claim: The high expression level of Ub might buffer some fitness defects.
source: Similarly, the high expression level of Ub might buffer some fitness defects.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the mutational tolerance of ubiquitin.

claim: The buffering might be exposed by chemical perturbations.
source: As an alternative approach to reducing expression, the buffering might also be exposed by chemical perturbations.
evidence: This is a hypothesis that motivated the experimental design.

claim: The sequence of Ub is subject to many constraints arising from interacting with diverse proteins while mediating the stress responses to distinct chemical perturbations.
source: Collectively, these results suggest that the sequence of Ub is subject to many constraints arising from interacting with diverse proteins while mediating the stress responses to distinct chemical perturbations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the literature review and experimental hypothesis.

claim: Expanding the set of environmental stresses might be able to explain the high sequence conservation of ubiquitin.
source: We suggest that expanding the set of environmental stresses, and improved measurement of smaller fitness defects, might be able to explain the high sequence conservation of ubiquitin, as different positions in the protein are important for interactions mediating the specific responses to a wide variety of perturbations.
evidence: This is a conclusion and suggestion for future work based on the experimental findings.

claim: Different positions in the protein are important for interactions mediating the specific responses to a wide variety of perturbations.
source: We suggest that expanding the set of environmental stresses, and improved measurement of smaller fitness defects, might be able to explain the high sequence conservation of ubiquitin, as different positions in the protein are important for interactions mediating the specific responses to a wide variety of perturbations.

claim: Small fitness defects that are undetectable by EMPIRIC may still be significant over evolutionary timescales.
source: Small fitness defects that are undetectable by EMPIRIC may still be significant over evolutionary timescales and are likely to similarly be enriched for certain chemicals (Boucher et al., 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to Boucher et al., 2014.
